column1: L1 is the single source of truth about the world as known at a point in time and answers exactly one question: what could the engine have known at asOf over [t, t + H_hot].
L1 answers its question in a way that makes the wrong answer structurally unreachable rather than merely discouraged.
L1's input is the cold tier plus warm frames plus derived artefacts, addressed by the run manifest, and its output is the BeliefSnapshot.
L1 is a pure read over immutable, content-addressed data with no writes, no clock, no randomness and no network.
Ingestion is a separate process and never runs inside a tick.
Ingestion is where almost all of the correctness of L1 is decided, because a fact stamped wrongly there is indistinguishable from a correct fact everywhere above.
The ingestion pipeline is source adapter, normalise, bitemporal stamp, validate, cold write.
Normalisation fixes units, signs, typed quantities, UTC and the 15-minute grid.
The bitemporal stamp is (validSlot, knowledgeTime, revisionOrdinal).
Ingestion validation applies the C0 universal invariants plus cadence and duplicate checks.
Cold writes are append-only Parquet in content-named batches.
Publication semantics are enforced as a schema rather than a habit, and every series is admitted only with a PublicationSemantics record.
knowledgeTimeRule is one of PublishedAt, ValidTimePlusLag, ArrivalObserved or Declared.
publicationLag is a SlotSpan used for the ValidTimePlusLag rule.
revisionPolicy is one of Never, Scheduled or Unbounded.
finalityLag is the number of slots after validSlot beyond which a value is final.
clockSkewBound is an upper bound on the source's own clock error.
latenessTolerance declares how late an arrival may be before it is an ingestion incident.
cadence is the expected publication interval and is the basis of gap detection.
fallbackChain is the ordered list of secondary sources.
Where knowledgeTime cannot be established exactly it is always rounded later and never earlier, as observedArrival plus clockSkewBound.
Because reads filter on knowledgeTime at most asOf, rounding later makes the engine know less than it did.
Rounding knowledgeTime later is a loss of realism in the conservative direction, while rounding earlier is lookahead, which is a fabrication of alpha rather than a loss of realism.
A source that cannot answer when a fact could first have been known is written to the cold tier under a quarantine prefix with a null knowledgeTime.
Quarantined partitions are readable by offline tooling and structurally unreachable from a production cursor.
The run manifest records the quarantined series, so a backtest states what it excluded rather than silently excluding it.
Late arrival, revision and restatement are the same mechanism: append a row.
A first publication writes one row at revisionOrdinal 0, visible from its knowledgeTime.

A late arrival — published on time but ingested late — writes one row at revisionOrdinal 0 visible from the publication instant, because lateness of ingestion is an operational fact and not a knowledge fact.
A revision or restatement writes one new row at the same validSlot with revisionOrdinal n+1, so the old value is visible before and the new value after, and both are permanently retained.
A retraction writes one tombstone row with quality Missing at revisionOrdinal n+1, and the field falls through the fallback ladder from that instant.
Nothing in the cold tier is ever updated or deleted in place.
Compaction rewrites files but never rows: it produces new content-named files and a new catalogue version, and the old catalogue remains resolvable for replay.
Append-only revisions buy the distinction Settlement needs between having been wrong and the data having been later corrected.
Collapsing revisions to last-value-wins destroys the ability to attribute a P&L gap between the forecastError bucket and a data restatement, and there is no way to recover it afterwards.
The watermark per source is the knowledgeTime up to which ingestion guarantees completeness, and the run's watermark is the minimum over the sources the manifest requires.
No snapshot may be built with asOf beyond the watermark.
Without the watermark rule a replay can read a series that had not yet been loaded, see less than the engine actually saw, and produce a result that is neither the live result nor reproducible.
The watermark violation is the mirror image of lookahead and is easier to miss, because it makes backtests look worse rather than better, so nobody investigates.
The watermark is itself a recorded artefact, part of the manifest, and is replayed with the run.
A backtest of 2024 uses 2024's watermark trajectory, including the days when a feed was six hours late.
The cold tier is laid out as series, then source, then valid_date partitions of content-named Parquet parts, with separate features and quarantine prefixes.
Cold rows are sorted within a file by (validSlot, knowledgeTime, revisionOrdinal).
A cold row carries validSlot, knowledgeTime, revisionOrdinal, scenarioIndex, value, provenance, quality and sourceId.
scenarioIndex is −1 for scalar series.
Cold values are float32 for forecasts and ensembles and float64 for money and SOC.
knowledgeTime is deliberately finer than SlotId, in microseconds since epoch.
Publication events do not align to quarter hours, and a gate that closes at 12:00:00 must not be beaten by a price published at 12:00:00.4 rounded down to the 12:00 slot.
Partitioning by valid_date rather than knowledge_date is chosen because the dominant access pattern is a forward replay over valid time.
Revisions scatter across knowledge time but land in the partition they describe, which is the one the reader wants.
A warm frame is a derived artefact reproducible from cold plus a FrameSpecHash, is not a second source of truth, and may be deleted and rebuilt at any time.
A frame is a single memory-mapped file with all offsets 64-byte aligned, carrying a 64-byte header, run pairs per slot, ascending knowledgeTime entries, scenario-major values and packed quality.
A frame's slotCount is not 96 but whatever the CivilCalendar says the frame's day contains: 92, 96 or 100.
A frame covers a local civil day, because every consumer that cares about day boundaries cares about local ones.
Resolving asOf inside a frame is: index the slot's run, binary-search knowledgeTime for the last entry at most asOf, read the value.
For the overwhelmingly common case of revisionPolicy Never, every run has length 1 and the search is a load.
The hot window is one instance per cursor, allocated at cursor open, never reallocated, and refilled in place per tick.
The hot window's ensemble array is ArrayPool-backed and flattened as series by scenario by slot, slot-contiguous.
HotWindow.Refill allocates nothing.
Slot-contiguous, scenario-major layout is chosen because the dominant hot-path operations are a weighted reduction across scenarios at a fixed slot and a scan across slots at a fixed scenario.
Making the slot axis contiguous keeps the fixed-scenario scan at streaming bandwidth and leaves the cross-scenario reduction as a strided gather with a fixed, prefetchable stride.
Refill strategy is per-series and derived from the declared publication semantics.
Consecutive ticks overlap by H_hot − 1 slots, so a ring buffer with a modular base index copies one slot per series rather than the whole window.
The ring-buffer refill is valid only for series with revisionPolicy Never, because a new asOf can change values at slots the window already holds.
Series that may be revised are fully refilled, and the split reads the same declaration ingestion enforced rather than being a heuristic.
Nothing in the read path is indexed by history.
The cold tier has zero resident bytes because it is never mapped by the tick loop.
The warm tier's resident bytes are a configured, LRU-bounded frame budget that does not grow with backtest length.
The hot tier's resident bytes are series times H_hot times S times value size plus small side arrays, and do not grow with backtest length.
With K = 8 ensemble series, S = 64, H_hot = 192 and float32, the hot ensemble is about 393 kB.
Scalar series, quality and knowledge-time arrays add well under 100 kB.
A four-year backtest touches about 140,000 ticks and the resident set at tick 140,000 is byte-for-byte the same as at tick 1.
Bounded resident memory is the property that makes the scenario axis affordable at all.
Bounded memory is fragile in exactly one way: any code that accumulates per-tick history reintroduces the growth term.
Seam recording is on-demand and streams to disk so that it does not reintroduce the memory growth term.
A replay advances a cursor and does not issue queries.
The cursor owns the hot window, the mapped frame set and the LRU.
Advance moves slotStart and asOf forward, both are monotone by default, and a backwards Advance is rejected.
At H_hot = 192, two days, the frame set covering the window is two or three frames per series.
Advancing maps any unmapped frame, registers it in the LRU, refills the hot window and bumps the generation.
LRU eviction is over a byte budget and not a frame count, because frame sizes differ by series and by DST day.
Evicting unmaps the frame while the OS page cache retains the pages, so re-mapping a recently evicted frame costs a syscall and no I/O.
The LRU manages address space and the page cache manages memory.
Prefetch runs when the cursor crosses a configured fraction of the current frame, mapping the next frame per series and advising WILLNEED on a background thread.
Prefetch is purely a performance concern and cannot affect output, because frames are immutable and content-addressed so a prefetched frame and a demand-mapped frame are the same bytes.
T3 asserts prefetch neutrality by running an audit day with prefetch disabled and comparing artefact hashes.
Sequential forward replay with prefetch on costs about zero frame maps per tick amortised and is bound by the memory bandwidth of the refill copy.
Sequential forward replay with prefetch off costs zero frame maps except a burst at each day boundary, on the critical path.
A backward seek inside the LRU budget costs zero frame maps and behaves as sequential.
A random jump costs one cold frame map per series and is bound by storage IOPS.
The production tick loop and the primary backtest are strictly sequential forward.

Sequential forward is the access pattern mmap plus page cache is best at: pages are read ahead by the kernel, touched once, and evicted in the order they were loaded, with no user-space bookkeeping and no copy into a managed heap.
Three harnesses need jumping cursors: sampled-day scenario analysis, the counterfactual re-runs behind the four-bucket decomposition, and targeted debugging of a single historical tick.
A jump invalidates the entire frame set, costing one cold frame map per series and a page-fault storm on first touch.
On a jump, throughput falls from sequential bandwidth to random-read IOPS: typically one to two orders of magnitude on spinning or networked storage and a factor of a few on local NVMe.
A harness that visits a set of ticks can visit them in slot order and is then sequential again with gaps, and this is the default in the harness rather than an option.
If the sampled day set's frames fit in the frame budget, the second pass is free.
A jumping harness is a research tool run on tens of days, not the production path run on years.

No global secondary index or row-oriented store is added to make jumping fast, because both would cost the sequential path that carries 99% of the work to accelerate a path that runs occasionally and is not latency-sensitive.
Adding an index for jumping would be the database-as-the-hot-path alternative ADR-004 already rejected, arriving by a side door.
The FeatureSpecHash is a hash over the complete derivation and not over the output.

The FeatureSpecHash covers featureType, generatorCodeRevision, canonically ordered hyperparameters, input series ids and their catalogue versions, the training asOf boundary and validRange, the tzdata version, and the generator seed.
A backtest cannot silently use a different feature definition than the one recorded, because the definition is the key.
A change to any artefact input — including tzdata and the seed — produces a different artefact rather than a quietly different result.
The run manifest pins every FeatureSpecHash in force, and reading an artefact whose spec hash is not in the manifest is a hard failure rather than a fallback.
The full joint scenario ensemble never reaches C1 directly and is refreshed daily on C_slow.
The reduced ensemble and weights reach C1 as scenarioWeights and the scenario-indexed arrays, refreshed daily on C_slow.
The fill-probability surface P(fill | product, priceBand, timeToGate, volume) reaches C1 as volumes only, refreshed on recalibration.
The price-impact curve mapping volume to expected price concession does not reach C1 and is for the quoting policy only.
The activation-probability model is exported as a PWL or lookup table and reaches C1 as activationUp and activationDn.
Peak and load climatology are quantile surfaces by calendar bucket used for ladder rung 4 imputation, refreshed seasonally.
The AW>0 indicator (24)¼ is a bool per slot, and scenario-indexed beyond the settled day-ahead horizon, refreshed on C_gate at day-ahead publication.
MW_month is a double per scenario per calendar month, derived per scenario on C_slow.
The value function is a materialised, content-hashed artefact produced by the slow loop that lives in L0 rather than L1, and L1 neither reads it nor carries it across C1.
Both delineation inputs are derived rather than ingested, and both are derived in ways that are easy to get subtly wrong.
AW drops to zero under § 51 and § 51b EEG on negative day-ahead prices, but the rule carries a duration condition, so the indicator for one quarter-hour depends on a run of neighbouring prices.
The (24)¼ indicator is computed by a small automaton over the day-ahead price series with the run-length threshold as configuration per EEG vintage.
For D+1 the AW>0 indicator is a realised parameter known at the day-ahead gate, and beyond that horizon it is scenario-dependent and carries the scenario axis like any other belief.
Plants on different EEG vintages can forfeit AW at different times.

The A5 collapse assumes a common EEG vintage, and the automaton is where a mixed estate would first become visible; it must refuse to emit a single site-level indicator in that case rather than silently picking one.
MW_month is a deterministic functional of national spot prices and national solar generation, both already dimensions of the joint ensemble, so it is computed inside each scenario.
A month with many negative-price hours has a lower MW_month, which raises the premium, while simultaneously lowering (30), which reduces the volume the premium applies to.
The two MW_month channels oppose each other and only a joint derivation can represent that.
The premium's floor at zero makes it convex in MW_month, so a point forecast understates it, most severely when MW_month sits near AW.
K is the number of uncertain series on the shared axis, S_gen the scenarios in the generated ensemble before reduction, and S the scenarios in the reduced ensemble.
Only the reduced ensemble crosses C1.
The weights invariant and the marginal-mean preservation invariant are checked at artefact write time and again at snapshot validation, because the artefact could be correct and the load path wrong.
The engine never recomputes a feature artefact online.

Exactly three operations on an artefact are permitted inside the tick loop: a bounds-checked lookup in a precomputed table, evaluation of a piecewise-linear function at a point, and a weighted reduction over the scenario axis with fixed partitioning.
Fitting, interpolating across a dimension the artefact does not tabulate, resampling and re-reducing an ensemble are all offline concerns.
A model too complex to export into one of the three permitted forms is too complex to be in the tick loop, and that is a finding about the model rather than a limitation of the layer.

LOB deltas are ingested at source fidelity into the cold tier, partitioned by productId and tradingDate, ordered by exchange sequence number, with sequence gaps recorded explicitly as tombstone rows rather than interpolated.
Raw order-book rows are never built into warm frames for a production cursor and never mapped by the tick loop.
Only idReliableVolumeBuy, idReliableVolumeSell and optionally idVolumeByPriceBand cross C1 from the order book, as volumes in kWh per slot.
No price field exists in the C1 liquidity section, which is the C1-side enforcement of the rule that fill probability constrains the Planner but never prices for it.
Reliable volume is defined as the volume q such that the probability of filling q within the residual window is at least θ, where θ is configuration and deliberately conservative.
Reliable volume is a quantile of a fitted surface rather than an expectation, because the Planner uses it as a bound and a bound that is right on average is wrong half the time.
The fill model is calibrated offline against the existing market simulator.

The calibration path replays recorded book state into the simulator at a recorded asOf, submits a grid of synthetic limit orders over product, price band, volume, time-to-gate and book-state bucket, records realised fill rate, partial-fill distribution and time-to-fill, fits P(fill), inverts to the θ-quantile reliable volume per slot, and content-hashes the result.
T4 characterisation reports realised versus predicted fill rate by price band, product and time-to-gate as a calibration curve rather than a scalar.
Whatever is calibrated against the simulator inherits the simulator's biases, and the gap between simulator-calibrated and venue-calibrated behaviour is a named risk.

The research-fidelity tier holds full LOB deltas, per-order events, sequence numbers and book reconstruction for calibration, high-fidelity replay, T4 and incident forensics, and is never in the tick loop.
The production-features tier holds reliable volume per slot and per band plus its QualityStamp, crosses C1, and is in the tick loop via the hot window.
The research/production split is enforced structurally: the two live in different frame families and a cursor is constructed with the production family only.
Reaching the raw book from the tick loop would require constructing a second cursor over the research family, which is a visible, reviewable code change rather than an accident of a stray query.
OPEN-3's resolution changes how much of the cold tier must hold raw book data and the shape of the production feature, but not the research/production split and not the C1 contract.
The hot-path discipline is normative for every assembly on the tick path: L1's read path, L2, L3's model construction and L5.
Struct-of-arrays is required for every slot- and scenario-indexed quantity, making reductions contiguous scans, enabling SIMD, and avoiding per-element header overhead.
Span and ReadOnlySpan are required for every slice crossing an internal boundary, giving zero-copy, no array allocation and bounds-check elision on the common loop shape.

ArrayPool.Shared is required for transient buffers with clearArray false and a deterministic return path, because the alternative is a per-tick LOH allocation for anything at least 85 kB, which the ensemble arrays exceed.
LINQ is banned anywhere in the tick loop because it allocates an enumerator and usually a closure per call and hides iteration order, which determinism requires to be fixed.
Per-slot and per-scenario object allocation is banned because H times S times K objects per tick is gen0 churn measured in hundreds of kB per tick.
Boxing of typed quantities is banned because it allocates and defeats the entire type discipline.
readonly struct plus in parameters are required for snapshot passing, to prevent silent defensive copies of a large struct at every call site.
async and Task are banned in the tick loop because they allocate a state machine and their presence implies an I/O dependency that must not exist on this path.
Dictionary lookup keyed by string is banned in the tick loop because of per-lookup string hashing and unordered iteration, and series and slot indices are resolved to int once at cursor open.
Every parallel reduction uses fixed partitioning, because floating-point summation order must not depend on core count or on the thread pool's dynamic partitioner.

A weighted mean over S = 64 scenarios partitioned by the default range partitioner sums in an order that depends on thread scheduling, the result differs in the last bits, the MILP takes a different branch, and two runs with identical manifests disagree.
The fix for partitioning non-determinism is to partition by a fixed block size derived from S alone and to reduce the partial sums in a fixed order.
A four-year backtest at quarter-hourly ticks is about 140,000 ticks.
A naive implementation materialising one double array per series and scenario allocates 512 arrays of 192 doubles, about 800 kB per tick, which is about 112 GB of gen0 traffic over a four-year run.
The same run against a preallocated, pooled hot window allocates zero bytes per tick after warm-up.
The solve itself is milliseconds and is dominated by the solver, which is native code the GC never sees.
The engine's own contribution is copies and reductions over a few hundred kB, so allocation rate and the resulting gen0 pauses are the throughput ceiling long before any arithmetic is.

Backtest throughput is the binding constraint on how fast the strategy can be improved, so the allocation discipline is the difference between a research loop measured in hours and one measured in days.
The six fallback rungs are applied per field with maxStale and Default taken from the C1 field tables.
Rung 1, primary source fresh, executes in the cursor read with provenance as published and quality Good.
Rung 2, primary source stale within maxStale, executes in the cursor read with quality Stale.
Rung 3, a secondary source from the fallbackChain, executes in the snapshot builder with quality Degraded.
Rung 4, model imputation by persistence, climatology or ensemble mean, executes in the snapshot builder artefact-backed with provenance and quality both Imputed.
Rung 5, the conservative default from the C1 field table, executes in the snapshot builder with provenance Default and quality Imputed.
Rung 6, no safe default, executes in the snapshot builder with provenance Default and quality Missing.
Ingestion never imputes, and rungs 3 to 6 are read-path operations.
Writing an imputed value into the cold tier would put invented data behind the same API as observed data and destroy the wrong-versus-corrected distinction.
The cold tier contains Imputed or Default provenance only where the source itself published an imputed value and declared it as such.
provenance and quality are not parallel enumerations: rungs 4 and 5 both yield quality Imputed and are distinguished by provenance.
Provenance is the finer discriminator and is what the risk mapping should key on when provenance and quality disagree.
maxStale is declared per field in C1 and is not always a duration: it is Slots(n), Gate(marketId) or None.
Under Slots(n) a field is stale when asOf minus knowledgeTime exceeds n slots.
Under Gate(marketId) a field is stale when a gate for that market has closed since knowledgeTime.
Under None a field is never stale, being structural data from the calendar.
Gate is the correct staleness semantics for daPrice and afrrCapPrice, because a day-ahead price belief from before the gate has been superseded by an event rather than merely being old.
Expressing gate staleness as a slot count would be either too lenient at 03:00 or too strict at 11:59.
Staleness is computed against asOf and never against a wall clock.
A field is critical when the C1 field table has Null = no and Default is an em dash.
criticalMissing is exactly the set of fields whose quality is Missing and which are critical.
The archetype of a critical field is socNow, which is measured and escalates rather than defaulting if telemetry is lost.
A field with Null = no and a declared conservative default is not critical, because rung 5 always succeeds for it, while a field with no safe default falls to rung 6 by construction.
C1 carries both criticalMissing as same-tick evidence and degradationMode read from L0 and therefore one tick old.
A non-empty criticalMissing implying mode at least DEFENSIVE is compatible with the one-tick-old mode only if L1 may raise the mode within the tick.
The C1 degradation mode is the maximum of the mode from L0 and the mode floor derived from criticalMissing.
L1 applies a monotone escalation floor derived from its own same-tick input: it can raise the mode and can never lower it.
De-escalation stays centrally governed and hysteretic.

The escalation floor does not violate ADR-006, because it is computed from L1's own inputs rather than read from a same-tick write by another component, and the evidence is published so the central mode computation sees it in the next tick's StateUpdate.
The C1 envelope, scalars and scenarioWeights are copied by value because they are tens to hundreds of bytes.
Quality stamps, criticalMissing and degradationMode are copied by value because they are small and consumers index them irregularly.
Slot- and scenario-indexed arrays are referenced as ReadOnlyMemory over hot-window buffers, because copying about 400 kB per tick serves no purpose.
Reserve product structure and tariff structure are referenced into an immutable, content-addressed calendar artefact because they never change within a run.
A handle — a cursor, a frame, anything that can be advanced or that aliases storage whose contents may change under the reader — is forbidden in a contract.
A read-only view over a buffer that is contractually immutable for the lifetime of the tick is permitted, and it is what makes the snapshot cheap.
BeliefSnapshot is a readonly struct carrying the envelope, ReadOnlyMemory views and a generation token, used in-process on the hot path.
BeliefSnapshotRecord is a fully materialised value with stable binary and JSON forms, used for seam recording, golden tests and cross-process replay.

C0's contract-is-a-value requirement is satisfied by the existence and byte stability of the record form and by the round-trip property that the record of a snapshot equals the record of its serialise-deserialise round trip.
Materialisation of the record form happens off the hot path, on audit days only.
The generation token makes the immutability claim checkable rather than aspirational: the cursor bumps the generation on every refill, the snapshot captures it, and every span accessor validates it.
A component that retains a snapshot past the end of its tick and dereferences it throws instead of reading whatever the next tick refilled.
In production builds the generation check is retained on the coarse accessors and elided inside inner loops.
The snapshot's content is completely determined by its derivation.

The snapshot content hash covers asOf, slotStart, slotCount, scenarioCount, ordered series ids, the frame content hash per series, the feature spec hash per artefact used, the scenario weights hash, the quality stamp digest, criticalMissing and degradationMode.
Because frames are immutable and content-addressed, hashing the derivation is exactly as discriminating as hashing the data, and it is O(series) instead of O(series × H_hot × S).
Two snapshots with equal derivation hashes hold identical arrays, and that implication is verified on audit days by computing the full data hash alongside and asserting agreement.
Frame resolution and mapping cost amortised about zero on the sequential path.
Hot-window refill costs one bounded copy of at most series times H_hot times S times 4 bytes.
The derivation hash costs O(series), tens of hashes.
Snapshot validation costs one linear scan over memory already hot in cache.
Snapshot construction allocates zero after warm-up.
The dominant term in building a snapshot is a sub-megabyte memcpy, which is why the layer can afford to build a fresh, fully validated snapshot on every tick rather than mutating one in place.

The no-lookahead property is tested two ways: a T6 re-run with every fact whose knowledgeTime exceeds t replaced by garbage asserting bit-identical artefact hashes, and a reflection test over the storage layer's public surface asserting no read method exists without an asOf parameter.
The reflection test is what keeps the lookahead audit true as the code grows, because it fails the moment someone adds a convenience overload.

Revision replay is tested on a series revised three times, asserting that a read at each of the four asOf points returns exactly the revision in force, that a forward-advancing cursor observes each revision exactly once and never a later one, and that the frame-resolved answer equals a naive cold-tier scan at every point.
Revision replay is extended with a cross-frame revision: a restatement arriving on day d for a validSlot on day d − 1.
The frame for the spring-forward day has 92 slots and the autumn day 100.
Frame boundaries sit at local midnight rather than at a fixed UTC offset.
A hot window spanning a DST transition still has slotCount equal to H_hot, because SlotId is a UTC quarter-hour count and is DST-independent: the frame count changes and the window length does not.

Frame boundary tests cover windows spanning two and three frames, a window starting exactly on a boundary, windows ending one slot before and one slot after a boundary, a series whose frame is absent for one day asserting the ladder is entered rather than an exception, and a frame whose contentHash does not verify asserting HALT.
Allocation counts are asserted by running N ticks after a warm-up of W and asserting the allocated bytes and gen0 collection count are unchanged.
The allocation assertion runs as a CI gate rather than an occasional benchmark, because allocation regressions arrive one LINQ call at a time and are invisible in correctness tests.
Ensemble coherence is tested by permuting the scenario axis of one series only and asserting that validation fails and that the snapshot's content hash changes.
A snapshot request with asOf beyond the watermark fails, and a quarantined series is unreachable from a production cursor with its presence in the manifest required for the run to start.
A jumping cursor and a sequential cursor visiting the same ticks must produce identical snapshot hashes, which catches state accidentally carried in the cursor across Advance.
The same audit day with prefetch on and off, and the same day on two machines with different core counts, must produce identical artefact hashes.
Every admitted series declares PublicationSemantics, quarantined series are unreachable from a production cursor and are named in the manifest, and violation is a HALT at manifest validation.
The cold tier is append-only with no row updated or deleted and retraction as a tombstone row, and violation is a HALT.
No snapshot is built with asOf beyond the run's ingestion watermark, and violation is a HALT.
Every derived artefact read has its FeatureSpecHash pinned in the run manifest, and violation is a HALT.
Hot-window refill and snapshot construction allocate zero managed bytes after warm-up, enforced as a CI gate.
Equal snapshot derivation hashes imply identical underlying arrays, and violation is a HALT checked on audit days.
No raw order-book row is reachable from a production cursor, and violation is a HALT.
Parallel reductions over the scenario axis use a fixed partitioning independent of core count and scheduler, and violation is a HALT verified by T3.
criticalMissing equals exactly the Missing fields with Null = no and no declared conservative default, and violation is a HALT.
An assigned knowledgeTime is never earlier than the source's true publication instant and uncertainty rounds later, and violation quarantines the source.
